nitric oxide synthase (NOS) 2 does not have a critical role on the development of left ventricular hypertrophy after chronic aortic constriction in mice.

the absence of nitric oxide synthase type 2 (N2S2) does not influence the development of hypertrophic cardiomyopathy after chronic pressure overload, but it does lead to impaired systolic function in the early phase of the disease.
NOS2 does play a role in the pathogenesis of pressure‐overload induced cardiac hypertrophy.

the role of NOS2 in the development of cardiac hypertrophy and dysfunction following pressure overload.
the development and progression of cardiac hypertrophy and heart failure in the mouse, and the role of nitric oxide (NO) and reactive oxygen species in these processes.
the role of nitric oxide synthase (NOS) in left ventricular ( LV ) remodelling and LV hypertrophy ( LVH ) following prolonged pressure overload.

NOS2 is not required for the development of LV remodelling and dysfunction following pressure overload.
